drivingQuestion: Does the jaw given to the priest stop at the upper ring of the windpipe, as the mishna says, or include the area of slaughter, as the baraita says?
outcomeNote: The objection is left standing at the close of this unit; it is answered at the opening of the next (chullin.sugya402).

segments.he: אֵיזֶהוּ לֶחִי – מִן הַפֶּרֶק שֶׁל לְחִי וְעַד פִּיקָּה שֶׁל גַּרְגֶּרֶת, וְהָתַנְיָא: נוֹטְלָהּ וּבֵית שְׁחִיטָה עִמָּהּ?
segments.en: § The mishna taught: «What is» definition of «the jaw?» It is «from the joint of the jaw» beneath the temples and below «until the upper ring of the windpipe.» The Gemara objects: «But isn’t it taught» in a baraita that when one removes the jaw from the animal to give to the priest, «he removes it and the area of slaughter» on the throat «with it?» The area of slaughter is beyond the upper ring of the windpipe.
